## TL;DR
- Conducted a read-only survey of the repository using three parallel subagents without modifying any files.

- **`oga-events`**: Manages event bounds, event normalization, presentation formatting, and real-time streaming wire records.
- **`oga-http`**: Provides Axum HTTP REST routes and web server endpoints for broker control, task actions, and web UI integration.
- **`oga-mcp`**: Implements an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server interface exposing broker tasks and discovery endpoints.
- **`oga-pricing`**: Calculates and estimates provider spend based on public model pricing data (such as `models.dev`) when spend is un-reported.
- **`oga-providers`**: Manages provider command arguments, transcript parsing, session structures, and CLI/ACP adapter specs.
- **`oga-routing`**: Handles task classification, routing policies, model selection criteria, and provider capability catalogs.
- **`oga-runner`**: Controls process spawning/execution lifecycles, output pipe streaming, process groups, and OS confinement/sandboxing.
- **`oga-service`**: Implements core orchestration logic for task dispatch, authorization, dependency resolution, handoffs, and state transitions.
- **`oga-store`**: Provides SQLite database persistence, schema management, transactional storage, and repository querying for the broker.
- **`oga-worktree`**: Manages Git worktrees, isolated task branch creation, git diff calculation, and branch lifecycle operations.

---

### B. Activity Domain (`web/src/domain/activity/`)

- **`index.ts`**: Core activity timeline composition module.
  - **Exported Types & Interfaces:** `ActivityComposition`, `ActivityEnding`, `ReasoningPulse`, `ActivityStatus`, `ActivityBlock`, `ActivityTurn`, `ActivitySegment`, `ActivityNode`, `ActivityCall`, `ActivitySubagent`, `HandoffBriefTier`, `HandoffBoundary`, `HandoffRun`, `Hop`.
  - **Exported Functions:** `compositionCalls`, `nodesCallCount`, `nodesDurationMs`, `turnDurationMs`, `callDurationMs`, `compositionHasThinking`, `withoutDuplicateHookCalls`, `normalizeAntigravityEvents`, `deriveTurnIds`.
  - **Exported Objects & Classes:** `ActivityStory`, `ActivityStoryProjection`.
  - **Exported Constants:** `SUBAGENT_STARTED_TITLE`, `SUBAGENT_FINISHED_TITLE`, `ACTIVITY_SKIPPED_TITLE`, `REASONING_TITLE`.
- **`index.test.ts`**: Unit test suite for activity domain composition (no exported functions/types).
- **`acp.test.ts`**: Unit test suite for ACP event normalization (no exported functions/types).
- **`fixtures/`**: Directory containing event fixture datasets (`antigravity-acp-probe.json`, `antigravity-run.jsonl`, `claude-acp-resumed.json`, `probe-rows.json`).

---

### C. Unreleased Changelog (`CHANGELOG.md`)

Lines under `## Unreleased`:
- Settings is roomier and easier to scan: sections are grouped with icons in the sidebar, each page has a clear title, and every setting sits on its own row with its switch or button on the right.
- OpenCode workers keep working when OpenCode 2 has taken over the `opencode` command: they find your OpenCode 1 install, and if there isn't one, the task stops straight away and says what to do instead of failing with an unrecognized flag. A worker can also point at a specific OpenCode 1 install.
- OpenCode 2 workers work again with OpenCode 2.0 and later, even when that install has also taken over the `opencode` command. Tasks, follow-ups, the model list with its effort levels, and continuing a task in a terminal all work, and a worker can point at a specific OpenCode 2 install.
- Picking a task from the list now puts you straight in its reply box.
- ⌘B (Ctrl+B on Windows and Linux) now shows or hides the task list, and puts you right in it so the arrow keys move between tasks.
- The reply box is simpler: task details and options now live behind the + button, so typing your next message is the only thing in the way.
- Settings can now pick the worker for you: turn on Choosing a worker, paste your TypeSafe key, and work you hand over without naming a worker lands on the one whose strengths fit what you asked for. Your own rules still catch anything it can't answer, and the task shows which worker was suggested and whether the work went there.
- Claude workers can now run newer models, like Opus 5.5, by using the Claude Code already installed on your machine instead of the older copy Oga shipped with.
- A task no longer fails with a confusing error when it starts just as Oga itself is starting up.
- The reply box no longer jumps when the note about continuing a paused task appears, and that note now lines up with the options under the box.
- Text in a task's activity log — command output, labels, and the response — now reads at one consistent size instead of jumping between sizes.
